note: ONE cut route for every hemisphere of every subject. Every landmark is coordinate-free: a parcel centroid, a parcel-border centroid, or a geodesic anchor. '<P1>_<P2>.._tip' is the vertex of that region geodesically farthest from EVERY border it has with another cortical parcel, i.e. the point of the region deepest away from the rest of cortex (TG_tip = the temporal pole). No rule uses a coordinate axis, so the cuts do not depend on how the head lies in the scanner and are mirror-symmetric between hemispheres by construction. The frontal cut TRACES the OFC/ACgG border (98-100 % of its length lies on it): running it as a shortest path instead sent it across the anterior cingulate and left 12-23 % of that area detached from the rest of itself on the flat map, which a cut must not do. The temporal cut is a sulcus-preferring path, 74-84 % of it inside sulci, because every border-anchored alternative ran over gyral crowns, detached 9-11 % of the amygdala instead of 2 %, and made the two animals agree less well. Apply with `mfa flatten --cut-recipe <this file>` (this file is the default).
slit_width_policy: recipe.slit_width is only the default/fallback. The slit width is a technical mesh parameter, not part of the anatomical route: the standard is the NARROWEST width that passes every quality gate on each hemisphere (1 boundary loop, 0 isolated vertices, 1 component, 0 flipped triangles, a well-defined anatomical display frame, hot_pack <= 3), chosen automatically with `--slit-width auto` (tries 1, 2, 3 in order) or fixed per hemisphere with `--slit-width lh=<a>,rh=<b>`.
